events.credibility_reason: Known only second-hand; reported community reservations; author, venue and text unlocatable; later work (Ismailescu-Lee 2025, Wikipedia, Andrade 2025) still treats the conjecture as open beyond degree 1.

Claims the first degree>=2 case (a landmark) with no uptake in ~3 years; scope shifted between versions to an almost-prime statement with rapid patch revisions; unrefereed EasyChair; later papers (Ismailescu-Lee 2025) state only the linear case is proved.

Redefines primality inside a private framework; decisive step asserted not argued; same author claims Goldbach, BSD, Beal and RH in the same series; no response in 16 months; Wikipedia and later papers still call it open.

Claims Schinzel H (implying twin primes) by Golomb's method, which the Rivoal/Hindry note reportedly says does not reach this; no engagement or citation in 16 months on a landmark problem; Wikipedia (Oct 2026) and later work still call it open; same author rapidly claims Bateman-Horn and Chowla by the same method; unrefereed and unread.
Same signals as the Schinzel claim, for an even stronger statement; unread, unrefereed, no uptake, part of a rapid series of famous-conjecture claims.
Unread claim of Chowla's conjecture in the same rapid series; different problem in any case.

why: The statement is universal over all admissible f, so averaged results (Skorobogatov-Sofos, Kravitz-Woo-Xu), polynomial-ring analogues (Bodin-Debes-Najib, Behajaina-Debes-Konig) and largest-prime-factor results (Li, Grimmelt-Merikoski) are variants, and Jones-Zvonkin's counts are instances. The only events claiming the conjecture or a case (Deloin, Sopin, AION, Xiao's Schinzel and Bateman-Horn) each carry several F10 signals together: landmark claims with no expert uptake over a long period, later papers and Wikipedia still calling the problem open, shifting scope or redefinition of primality, and serial claims of famous conjectures. Close call: Xiao's Schinzel claim was never read, so its argument has no identified error; it is set aside on the combination of silence, the reported unsuitability of Golomb's method, and the author's parallel claims rather than on any specific flaw. No AI system did mathematics in any event.
doubts: Xiao's Preprints.org papers and Sopin's final PDF were unreadable to the researcher; the not_credible calls rest on context, not on reading the arguments. Stanley Yao Xiao 2024's first posting date is unknown (year-only). Deloin's scope is unknown; recorded as a whole claim per the second-hand report.
